# Unify dock preview customization under one Neo owner

## Context

The [extensibility audit](https://github.com/neomjs/neo/issues/18304#issuecomment-5560546655) and [independent reproduction](https://github.com/neomjs/neo/issues/18304#issuecomment-5560658524) show a real disagreement: overriding `Preview.ratioToSizes` produces a 25% rendered fraction while `Preview.previewToOperation` still emits a 50/50 split. This is one bounded ownership cut within #18304.

## The Problem

`model/PreviewContract.mjs` exports lexical functions without a Neo identity. The renderer exposes competing policy wrappers, while direct drop consumers import the converter independently. Customization therefore reaches only part of the preview-to-operation path.

## The Architectural Reality

`Base.applyOverwrites` installs method/default overrides on the instance path. A fresh-process Base singleton probe confirmed that internal method dispatch observes a `Neo.overwrites` override and the exported instance is its registered namespace identity. Merely registering static wrappers or keeping captured function aliases would preserve the split.

The model folder already owns the pure preview grammar; this work changes its ownership/dispatch, not the grammar or window lifecycle. The earlier operator concern in #18064 / PR #18061 supplies the override-reach precedent; that guideline/guard ticket does not implement this module cut.

## The Fix

Convert the existing `PreviewContract.mjs` into one `Base`-derived singleton registered as `Neo.dashboard.dock.model.PreviewContract`. Its methods own validation, candidate validation, split normalization and conversion, and call other policy methods through `this`.

Move pure ratio-derived helpers to that owner. Remove competing pure-policy wrappers from `interaction/Preview.mjs`; update every production caller to reach the owner dynamically, including callback entry points. No retained named-function compatibility layer or aliases capturing policy methods.

Keep schema strings, placement vocabulary, explicit-ratio meanings, plain DTO results, and fail-closed behavior unchanged. Document the one supported customization point.

## Contract Ledger

| Surface | Authority | Behavior | Refusal/default | Docs | Evidence |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| New registered preview-policy owner | Base overwrite path; #18304 audit | One realm-local singleton, replaceable methods reached by all policy calls | Existing defaults retained | Class JSDoc | Namespace identity and overwrite tests |
| Renderer and direct drop callers | ADR 0029 preview → operation path | Same policy result reaches rendered fraction and semantic conversion | Invalid/rejected preview returns null | Renderer and owner JSDoc | Real overwrite consistency control |
| Runtime preview DTO | Existing PreviewContract grammar | Schema, item/group placement and explicit ratio remain unchanged | Existing validation refusals | Existing model reference as needed | Current grammar/producer tests |

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] The owner has a real Neo namespace identity and Base overwrite support; internal policy calls use that owner.
- [ ] Production callers and callback adapters dynamically invoke it; competing renderer policy wrappers and named-function exports are removed.
- [ ] A real `Neo.overwrites` customization reaches both the rendered fraction and converted/applied split for an omitted ratio; a pre-fix control demonstrates the disagreement.
- [ ] Explicit ratios, before/after and edge placements, item/group previews, rejection behavior and non-mutation of input DTOs retain their defined behavior.
- [ ] Focused preview/producer/indicator/drop tests and the unit suite pass; JSDoc/generated class hierarchy identify the new owner and customization path.

## Out of Scope

VesselConversion and other state-machine conversions, Workspace decomposition beyond updating this policy's call sites, native lifecycle/geometry repairs, new preview kinds or schemas, general lint/skill changes, and any changes to merged PR #18383.

## Avoided Traps

A registered wrapper around lexical helpers; two competing customization owners; converting every PascalCase module in one PR; preserving obsolete exports for historical callers; using passing default behavior as proof that customization works.

Decision Record impact: aligned-with ADR 0029; no wire or drag-protocol amendment.
Decision Record: existing ADR 0029 remains authoritative.
